descriptions.preferred: The spring foliage is the most outstanding feature of this cultivar. The color is difficult to describe, but it could be classed as a deep shrimp pink. It is very distinct and attracts much attention. It is a thrill to see this plant in its spring and early summer glory. During the summer the foliage turns a good tone of green, and some leaves are slightly variegated with minute flecks or speckles of light tones. The new growth which comes in late summer or early fall is scarlet. The leaves are near typical palmatum with five, or sometimes seven, lobes and 4-5 cm long and 5-6 cm wide. The leaf is divided halfway to two-thirds of the way to the leaf base. The lobes are ovate, tapered, and very slightly toothed. Many leaves develop a slight crinkling, not lying in a perfectly flat plane. The petioles are slender, reddish pink, and about 4 cm long. I had the pleasure of seeing Sir Harold Hillier's fine specimen plant at the Hillier Gardens and Arboretum, Romsey, Hampshire, England. Viewed during the first week in June, it was in its glory of rich pink tones. In my opinion, it rivaled many flowering shrubs. care.cultivation: Grow in a moist but well-drained soil. Water in summer if necessary. Leaf colour is best in partial shade, although full sun can be tolerated. Leaf scorch can be caused by lack of soil moisture or excessive exposure. See Japanese maple cultivation
care.propagation: Propagate by grafting or softwood cuttings

resistance.pest: May be susceptible to Acer gall mite, aphids , caterpillars and horse chestnut scale
resistance.disease: May be susceptible to Verticillium wilt , Acer leaf scorch and honey fungus

rhs_zh.description: 一种生长缓慢、株型浓密的落叶灌木，春季叶片掌状裂，呈显著的深粉色；夏季转为不同深浅的绿色。 夏季或秋季抽发的新梢叶为鲜红色，与绿色老叶形成对比。 虽然该品种可耐全日照，但在半阴环境下色彩表现最佳。
